page.overview:
Who is Undead?

The undead are beings in mythology, legend, or fiction that are deceased but behave as if they were alive. A common example of an undead being is a corpse reanimated by supernatural forces, by the application of either the deceased's own life force or that of a supernatural being (such as a demon, or other evil spirit). The undead may be incorporeal (ghosts) or corporeal (mummies, vampires, skeletons, and zombies).

The undead are featured in the belief systems of most cultures, and appear in many works of fantasy and horror fiction. The term is also occasionally used for real-life attempts to resurrect the dead with science and technology, from early experiments like Robert E. Cornish's to future sciences such as "chemical brain preservation" and "cryonics." While the term usually refers to corporeal entities, in some cases (for example, in Dungeons & Dragons), the term also includes incorporeal forms of the dead, such as ghosts.

entity.name: Undead
entity.short_description: These beings were typically skeletal-looking creatures who were forever to be tormented within their fiery homeworld. Some were capable of ripping apart bloody chunks from their body and throwing them at their enemies…
entity.description:
These beings were typically skeletal-looking creatures who were forever to be tormented within their fiery homeworld. Some were capable of ripping apart bloody chunks from their body and throwing them at their enemies as a form of projectile attack. When encountering living creatures, the Undead often converged on the source of fresh meat in order to devour it. Typically, they ambushed prey by suddenly emerging from the ground.

Liu Kang and Kung Lao encountered and defended themselves against numerous undead enemies in the Living Forest, the Soul Tombs, the Sea of Blood in the Wastelands of Outworld, and even the Netherrealm itself.

Shujinko encountered numerous undead beings within the city of Nekros as well as the burning plains outside.
